newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: JugoRosGas to expand Serbian gas pipeline network.
newsitem.headline: JugoRosGas to expand Serbian gas pipeline network.

text.p: Yugoslav-Russian gas trade and transport joint venture JugoRosGas will start building a new gas pipeline in central Serbia by the end of 1997, Belgrade daily Politika said on Friday.

"The pipeline linking Pojate, Nis and Dimitrovgrad (at the Yugoslav-Bulgarian border), is the first JugoRosGas investment and will be finished by the year 2000," assistant to the general manager of the NIS Serbian oil company Milan Mladenovic was quoted as saying.
The 172 kilometres (107 miles) stretch, estimated to cost around $105 million to build, should help secure more regular gas supplies from Russia, now flowing to Serbia across Hungary.

Expansion of the gas network in Serbia by 2000, included completion of the Vrbas-Kula-Crvenka-Sombor-Apatin stretch (in Vojvodina), construction of a gas reservoir in Banatski Dvor and completion of the stretch in western Serbia, Mladenovic said.
"The news signalled that JugoRosGas will take over all projects for expanding gas network in Serbia south of the Danube," Politika said.
There was no one immediately available for comment at JugoRosGas.
JugoRosGas was founded in June 1996, with Russia's Gazprom holding a 50 percent stake, while the remainder is divided among Serbia's Progres, Progres Gas Trading, NIS and Beobanka.

Yugoslavia plans to construct 1,537 kilometres of gas pipelines to increase the network to 3,000 kilometres by the year 2010 and supply 450,000 households with gas. To develop the network, Yugoslavia needs $413 million by the end of the century.
In 1990, the country consumed 2.8 billion cubic metres of gas, hoping to raise consumption to 6.2 billion in 2010.
